title: Hornbeam: Ancient Hornbeams You Can Visit
meta_description: A hedge species left free to grow: a 19-metre giant in Aarhus, a Copenhagen tree stripped of pacifiers each November, a Nijmegen elder by a sequoia.
intro: Carpinus betulus is Europe's shear-proof hedge tree, planted by the thousand for its density and its patience under a blade, which is why a hornbeam left alone to grow into its full, fluted-trunked shape reads as a surprise. Three stand mapped here, none of them clipped. Aarhus's, in Moesgard's landscape garden, was measured in 2022 at nineteen metres, taller than the species usually reads, its only flaw a little shade thrown by nearby planes. Copenhagen's, in Frederiksberg Have, carries no age or measurement on the Danish national register at all, only a name, Suttetraeet, the pacifier tree, harvested bare every November when local toddlers tie up the dummy they have agreed to give up. Nijmegen's grows a few metres from Krayenhoffpark's giant sequoia, roughly the same age at around 120 years, the only shade in its railway district older than the houses around it.
